title: Preservation of a pair square under stage refinement
statement: Let X,Y,Yprime,Z be schemes [def-pc-scheme], U an open cover of X, and q:Y -> X, qprime:Yprime -> X, r:Yprime -> Y with r followed by q equal to qprime. Let p:Z -> Y, pprime:Z -> Yprime, t:Z -> X satisfy p followed by q=t, pprime followed by qprime=t, and pprime followed by r=p. Fix modules N_a on U_a, a module M on Z, and isomorphisms from t-pullbacks of N_a to the restrictions of M [def-pc-base-change]. If a pair map on the q-pulled cover commutes with the transition of M on the p-limit overlap, using the canonical iterated comparisons [def-pc-local-overlap-transitions, def-pc-overlap-pair-canonical-comparisons], then there is a pair map on the qprime-pulled cover commuting on the pprime-limit overlap, using the corresponding canonical comparisons. No finite presentation, quasi-coherence, affineness or directed limit assumption is made.

proof.text: Take the given pair map phi. Construct rho by overlapRefinementHom. Its two projection equations give the cover refinement and the canonical module isomorphism c, defined by pullbackCompOfEq. Construct delta on each iterated limit chart by pullback.lift of the later Z projection and the later stage-chart projection followed by rho; the equality hp and rho cover-projection equation prove the lift condition. Its two projection equations are pullback.lift_fst and pullback.lift_snd.

proof.text: Apply overlap_pair_square_chart_transport to the chosen phi, its square, the explicitly constructed rho,c,delta and their projection equations, and the comparison-family equality. It proves the square for an explicit refined map. Introduce that map as the existential witness. The private existential helper only packages this explicit formula to keep elaboration from unfolding the concrete sheaf pullbacks.

lean.statement:
theorem overlap_pair_map_refinement_persistence
    {X Y Y' Z : Scheme.{u}} (U : X.OpenCover.{u})
    (q : Y ⟶ X) (q' : Y' ⟶ X) (r : Y' ⟶ Y) (hr : r ≫ q = q')
    (p : Z ⟶ Y) (p' : Z ⟶ Y') (t : Z ⟶ X)
    (h : p ≫ q = t) (h' : p' ≫ q' = t) (hp : p' ≫ r = p)
    (N : (a : U.I₀) → (U.X a).Modules) (M : Z.Modules)
    (e : ∀ a, (Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom t a)).obj (N a) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((U.pullback₁ t).f a)).obj M)
    (a b : U.I₀) :
    let V := U.pullback₁ q
    let A := fun d ↦ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom q d)).obj (N d)
    let W := V.pullback₁ p
    let D := (modulesPseudofunctor.toDescentData W.f).obj M
    let ε := overlapIteratedComparison U q p t h N M e
    (∃ φ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (V.f a) (V.f b))).obj (A a) ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd (V.f a) (V.f b))).obj (A b),
      overlapPairSquare V A p D ε a b φ) →
    let V' := U.pullback₁ q'
    let A' := fun d ↦ (Scheme.Modules.pullback (U.pullbackHom q' d)).obj (N d)
    let W' := V'.pullback₁ p'
    let D' := (modulesPseudofunctor.toDescentData W'.f).obj M
    let ε' := overlapIteratedComparison U q' p' t h' N M e
    ∃ φ' : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst (V'.f a) (V'.f b))).obj (A' a) ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.snd (V'.f a) (V'.f b))).obj (A' b),
      overlapPairSquare V' A' p' D' ε' a b φ'
